summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue fell to INR56 crore from INR90 crore as Evonile moved off single-customer model; INR83 crore one-time items booked.
summary.overview: Evonile Pharma (formerly Novartis India) reported its first results call after change of control, with Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR56 crore versus INR90 crore a year earlier, including INR41 crore from a major customer in the base period. Management attributed the decline to a one-time revenue correction and transition effects, not to weaker underlying demand. Adjusted operating EBITDA was negative INR16 crore for the quarter (INR19 crore for H1), with employee costs up to INR14 crore from INR5 crore as own field force and corporate team were built. Reported results include INR83 crore of one-time items: a INR68 crore exceptional item (INR61 crore from terminating exclusive promotion rights and inventory purchase arrangements with one large customer) and about INR15 crore of transition and Minipress XL acquisition costs within other expenses.

segments.name: Minipress XL (cardiology, acquired from Pfizer)
segments.commentary: Market-leading cardiology brand with more than 50% market share, acquired in the quarter. Market grew about 9% historically versus about 6% for the brand; about 300 of the planned 900 MRs are allocated to it.

segments.name: Ophthalmology (Accentrix and Pagenax, in-licensed)
segments.commentary: Exclusive distribution and promotion agreement signed in the quarter for a retina portfolio, adding ophthalmology to six priority therapies (cardiology, pain management, wellness, transplant, gynecology, neurosciences).

segments.name: Legacy brands (Voveran, Methergene, Calcium Sandoz, myFORTic)
segments.commentary: Management says each brand holds the number one position in its covered market; the brands were under-promoted and sales were largely to a single customer before the change of control.

guidance_outlook: Stable run-rate to be read from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; management said the stabilised base is around INR600 crore organically, to be doubled over 5-6 years, with acquisitions additional.
Management said FY28 revenue would grow on the stabilised base and would be above INR600 crore, though it also cited a base of around INR150 crore as a stabilisation marker.
Gross margin changes expected to be visible only from Q1 FY28, from product mix and new sourcing; bridging stock currently carried.
About INR15-20 crore of further one-time costs expected in Q3 FY27, with a more stable cost structure by Q4.
Incremental run-rate expense of about INR45-50 crore per quarter versus the Q1 base once fully stable (Q4 comparison), per CFO.
Net debt to be significantly reduced by March 31, 2027 via a rights issue; exact finance cost plan to follow once the rights issue plan is finalised.
Industry growth expected within 8-10% long-term (volume 3-4%, price 5-6%, new introductions 1-2%).
capex_capacity: Over 20 CFAs onboarded, giving a nationwide distribution network and direct control of supply chain from October 1.
Dedicated therapy-aligned field force planned at about 900 MRs, using experienced hires only; hiring expected to be substantially complete by end Q3 or beginning Q4 FY27.
Own accounting, HR and field-reporting systems set up, moving away from global systems.
New product introductions to teams expected from late Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; brand extensions and lifecycle management planned.
demand_pricing: Management said Q2 revenue decline reflects a one-time correction and transition, not underlying demand change.
Legacy brands had limited promotion and relied on doctor loyalty; majority of sales previously to a single customer.
Minipress XL: brand grew about 6% versus market about 9%; management expects to outgrow the market with a dedicated team, though one or two quarters are needed to scale.
Management expects the revenue run-rate to start reflecting in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with DRL Life products and Rover referenced in an audience question but no specific figures given.

qa_highlights.question: How much MR strength is in place now, and how much is allocated to Minipress?
qa_highlights.answer: Hiring is ongoing with experienced industry hires only; everyone should be on board by end Q3 or beginning Q4 FY27. About 300 of the planned 900 MRs will promote Minipress.

qa_highlights.question: Amortisation period for the Minipress goodwill?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it will be amortised over 20-25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Expected IPM growth over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-range industry growth has been within 8-10%, built from volume 3-4%, price 5-6% and new introductions 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the business lose Minipress share during transition, given no Pfizer field force was taken over?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of growing the brand; it will take one or two quarters to scale the team and promotion.

qa_highlights.question: Where will growth come from to double revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Three levers: legacy brand growth under new ownership, brand extensions and lifecycle management, and new products for the same specialists.

qa_highlights.question: What one-time costs are expected in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15-20 crore in Q3 FY27, with cost structure stabilising by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the finance cost and net debt expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost about INR15 crore in Q3 and INR10-15 crore in Q4; debt to be significantly reduced by March 31, 2027 via a rights issue, with the exact plan to be announced later.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 revenue be above INR600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the INR600 crore figure is the stabilised base; FY28 is expected to grow above it.

risks_watch: Revenue run-rate is still unclear; management points to Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 as the stable base, and Q2 revenue fell about 38% YoY.
Further one-time costs of INR15-20 crore expected in Q3 FY27.
Incremental field force and corporate cost ramp (about INR45-50 crore per quarter) ahead of revenue, with adjusted EBITDA already negative.
Gross margin benefit from sourcing efficiencies delayed until Q1 FY28 because of bridging and existing stock.
Rights issue and debt reduction plan not yet detailed; finance cost guidance depends on it.
Minipress retention through transition without Pfizer's field force.
Dependence on new hires reaching full strength by end Q3 or beginning Q4 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategic progress (distribution, portfolio, board) but cautious and non-committal on near-term numbers, repeatedly deferring to Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 for a stable base. Gave few hard numbers on growth beyond the INR600 crore base and avoided brand-level targets.
key_quotes: In just a few months since the change of control, we have moved from a single customer model to an independent company with its own distribution network, which markets its own brands.
So Q2 is the quarter in which the old model ended and a new one began.
These are transition effects. They do not reflect any change in the underlying demand for our brands.
